instructions: Mince half of the onion. Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat, add the onion and cook for 6 minutes, until it's golden. Transfer it to a large bowl and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, shred half of the cabbage and put it in a bowl in the fridge.
Add the beef, pork, 2 tbsp of the panko, 1 tbsp water, 1 of the eggs, the nutmeg, salt and pepper to the cooled onion. Knead by hand for 2 minutes, until the mixture is pale and sticky.

Divide the mixture into 6 portions. Roll each into a ball and toss it from hand to hand a few times to knock the air out. Flatten each into an oval patty about 3/4 inch thick. Put them on a plate and chill for 30 minutes.
Set out three plates: the flour on one, the remaining 2 eggs beaten on another, and the remaining 1 1/2 cups panko on the third. Coat each patty in flour, then egg, then press the panko on firmly.

Pour the frying oil into a heavy pot at least 3 inches deep and heat it over medium heat to 340°F. No thermometer? Drop in a pinch of panko: it should sizzle steadily and turn golden in about 30 seconds.
Lower in 2 or 3 patties. Leave them alone for 2 minutes, then flip and cook the other side for 3 minutes, until deep golden. Transfer them to a wire rack. Fry the rest in batches.
You're cooking the cutlets to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut the first one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Taste the first cutlet. If it's flat, sprinkle a pinch more salt over the rest while they're hot.
Serve the cutlets with the shredded cabbage and the tonkatsu sauce.
method_notes: Just One Cookbook cooks the onion first, kneads it into a beef and pork mixture with panko, milk, egg and nutmeg, chills the patties, and deep-fries them at 340°F. Japanese Cooking 101 skips cooking the onion and chills after breading. This one follows Just One Cookbook, with water in place of the milk to keep it dairy-free.
